items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: I'd break my neck to go over there and listen to them... I can't recall exactly what it was for, but as far as I can recall, it was just a parade.

ctx.x: Well, let's see. We're going to talk about a whole lot of different things, like I'd gotten a letter from Laurie Wright, and he wanted a little more information on Lewis Armstrong. Where did you first hear Louis Armstrong?

Well, as far back as I can remember, when I was a little kid, when this particular group of boys would parade on the streets, I'd break my neck to go over there and listen to them. And sometimes they came right down to San Antonio Street, which was about, well, in between the two blocks that I lived. I lived on Robinson and the parade would come down San Antonio Street. I don't know, I don't know, they had a hymn there. How did that happen? What were they doing? Well, just parading, I imagine. I can't recall…
